entries.title: record the R6 deletion's measurement
entries.body:
* docs(wp19): recount self/ and order the test job's steps as ci.yml runs them

MASTER_PLAN §4 now gives `self/` as 64 modules and 35,601 lines, with the
commands that count them. wp10-ci's `test (ubuntu-latest)` row lists

* docs(wp19): record the R6 deletion's measurement

The R6 row of wp19-stage0-retirement.md and the M6 row of MASTER_PLAN.md
had a placeholder where the measurement of the deletion was to go. It is
now there, dated: the undegraded `npm test` on `main` at `ad02409`, the
published package's file count, `npm run check` failing when a

entries.title: let nish-cmp remove each compiler's own version from the DWARF producer
entries.body:
A `-g` build records `producer: "nish <version>"`. nish-cmp compares the
last release against HEAD, and HEAD carries the next version from the
commit that bumps it, so every release turned the seven `dbg_*` cases red:
on the release pull request itself, and on `main` and every branch after
it until the release was published and became the seed. That is what held
0.7.0 back.

nish-cmp now removes each side's *own* version, as its `--version` prints
it, and only inside a `producer:` string, the way it already removes each
side's own package root. A candidate that records any version but its own
still differs. `selfCheckVersions` drives the rewrite over fabricated inputs
on every run and from `npm test`, and the summary counts the files that
needed it. `tests/run.js`'s `normaliseProducer` already does the same for
the goldens.
metrics: 514/514 programs agree against the v0.6.0 seed, 7 equal after each compiler's own producer version, 0 undeclared (was 507/514, 7 undeclared)

entries.title: prove bounds through toI32(length) and compile std/text silent
entries.body:
* perf(checker): prove bounds through toI32(length) and compile std/text silent

The bounds proof now reads the builtin `toI32(w.length)` as `w.length`.
That is the hoist a program has to write to compile in both number
modes: under `--number-mode f64` a `.length` is an `f64`, so
`const n: i32 = toI32(s.length)` is the only spelling an `i32` cursor
can be compared against. It now proves what `const n = s.length` proves,
in the hoist, in a loop condition and in a length guard. It is sound in
both modes: in i32 mode the conversion is the identity, and in f64 mode
it is a saturating `fptosi` of an exact integer, which answers the
length or less and never a negative. Only the builtin counts. A user
function named `toI32` wins over the builtin and may answer anything, so
it proves nothing. The builtin converts inline and calls nothing, so,
unlike any other call, it no longer drops the array-length facts. A
second hoisted `toI32(ys.length)` used to undo the first.

With that, and four local rewrites in `std/text.ts`, a program that
imports `nish/text` compiles with no performance warning from the
library, where every import used to print ten. The rewrites are guards
that always hold and prove a `substring` bound (`splitLines`,
`splitWhitespace`, `replaceAll`), and two length tests in place of a
ternary minimum in `firstDifference`. The behaviour is unchanged. Those
checks are proven away, not hidden: the library's IR goes from six
bounds-check sites to one (in `trimEnd`, at a computed index, which was
never reported) and from 40 clamp intrinsic calls to 28.

Measured: std/text.ts warnings on an importer, 10 -> 0 in i32 mode and 10 -> 0 in f64 mode
Refs: docs/LANGUAGE.md#element-access, docs/IR_COOKBOOK.md
Tests: tests/cases/perf_bounds_toi32, tests/cases/perf_bounds_toi32_f64, tests/cases/perf_bounds_toi32_loop, tests/cases/perf_bounds_toi32_user

* test(self): regenerate the corpus stores for the toI32 bounds cases

`tests/self/goldens/checked.txt` gains the four new
`perf_bounds_toi32*` programs and the `str_bounds_toi32` cookbook
snippet. `checked_self.txt` moves only inside `self/bounds.ts`, for its
new function and the lines after it. `tests/differential/goldens/unfrozen.txt`
registers the four new cases, which have no frozen rewrite. Each file was
written by its own tool (`node tests/self/goldens.js --update`,
`node tests/differential/goldens.js --update`), and the diff was read
before it was committed.

* refactor(checker): name the calls that call nothing, and guard std/text on its hoisted length

The walk and the loop-effect scan now ask one predicate, `callsNothing`,
which call leaves the array-length facts standing (`charCodeAt` and the
builtin `toI32`), so the two cannot drift apart. The `splitLines` and
`splitWhitespace` guards compare `start` strictly against the hoisted
`length` rather than converting `text.length` again: the strict test
goes through the hoist the same way the loop condition does, still
always holds, and costs one compare. `tests/self/goldens/checked_self.txt`
moves with the lines of `self/bounds.ts`.

Tests: tests/cases/perf_bounds_toi32, tests/cases/perf_bounds_toi32_f64

* test(self): declare the toI32 bounds proof's nish-cmp differences

`tests/nish-cmp.js` fails on any IR difference from the last release that
`DECLARED` does not name. This change moves 16 files on purpose, and each
now has a narrow entry, one program and one file, with the sentence
saying why:

- the new `perf_bounds_toi32*` cases and the `str_bounds_toi32` cookbook
  snippet;
- `text.ll` in every `std/text` importer;
- `testing.ll` in every `std/testing` importer, whose own
  `toI32(x.length)` hoists are now proven;
- `main.ll` of the two `std_text` programs.

Each entry names the words `CHANGELOG.md` now carries under
`[Unreleased]`. The 7 `dbg_*` differences, the `producer` string left by
the 0.7.0 bump, are not this change's and stay undeclared.

Refs: tests/nish-cmp.js

entries.title: constrained type parameters (WP18 G6)
entries.body:
A generic function, class or interface may now constrain a type parameter
with a declared class or interface: `<T extends Shape>`, or an instantiation
with its arguments written out, `<T extends Container<i32>>`. Through a `T`
the template may read, write and call exactly the constraint's members, and
every instantiation is checked against the constraint where it was
requested: at the call that inferred it, after `new`, in an annotation, a
field, an array element, a `Result` payload, a nested instantiation or an
`implements` target. A type argument satisfies a constraint when it is the
constraint itself or a class that `implements` it.

The lowering does not change. `areaOf<T extends Shape>` at `T = Circle` is
still its own `define` reading field 0 of `%struct.Circle`, with no bitcast
to `%struct.Shape` and no vtable, and every existing golden is byte-identical.

Member access is decided by where a value came from, not by its type.
During an instantiation `T` is already `Point`, so each value carries the
type its template wrote (its "origin"), and `p.x` is refused only when `p`'s
origin is a type parameter. At `T = Point`, `<T>(p: T, q: Point)` refuses
`p.x` and accepts `q.x`. Origins follow a value through locals, `new Box<T>`,
array literals and elements, fields and methods of a generic class, a
`Result`'s payload and a generic call that hands its argument back; an
expression kind added later fails closed. A refusal is reported once per
template, however many instantiations reach it. docs/wp18-generics.md §15.6
records the mechanism and the alternatives that were set aside.

A constraint that is not a class or interface (NL2327), or that mentions a
type parameter (NL2326), is refused at the declaration. An unsatisfied
constraint is NL2328, a member of an unconstrained parameter NL2329, and a
member the constraint does not declare NL2330. The old "not supported yet"
refusal is gone and its code, NL2294, is retired. The eight new programs the
v0.6.0 seed cannot parse are declared to nish-cmp.

BREAKING CHANGE: reading, writing or calling a member through an
unconstrained type parameter is now refused (``Cannot read `x` of `T`: an
unconstrained type parameter has no members``). It used to compile whenever
every instantiation happened to have the member. The fix is to name the
members with a constraint, `<T extends Point>`, where `Point` is a class or
interface that declares them.

entries.title: give each differential run its own working directory
entries.body:
The differential runner builds and runs every whole program eight at a
time, and every run shared the repository root as its working directory.
`io_nish_import` and its twin `io_nish_import_global` both write
`build/test/io_nish_import.txt` and read it back. They have to use the
same path, because `tests/run.js` requires the two to emit identical IR.
When one twin truncated the file while the other was reading it, the read
came back empty and the comparison failed at random: 2 runs in 40 on the
io_nish_import pair alone.

Each side of each program (the native binary and the Node rewrite) now
runs in `build/test/differential/<name>/<side>-cwd`. That directory is a
stand-in for the repository root: it has a private `build/`, with the
empty `build/test/` and `build/test/differential/` the corpus assumes,
and every other top-level entry is a symlink back to the checkout. So a
program that reads a checked-in file by a root-relative path, as
`corpus/io_streams` does, still finds it, and anything a program writes
under `build/` stays private to that run. No source file changes, which
matters because the frozen rewrites hash their sources. The native and
Node runs no longer see each other's leftovers either.

A new check in `tests/run.js` asserts that the twins' scratch files
landed in their own directories. It fails on every run if the isolation
is removed, where the race it replaces failed only occasionally.
metrics: io_nish_import pair at --jobs 16, 3 failures in 300 runs before, 0 in 900 after; full corpus at --jobs 8, 0 unexpected failures in 20 runs
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: hold std/ and examples/ to zero performance warnings and ratchet self/
entries.body:
`npm test` now fails when anything that ships carries a performance
warning. Every `std/` module and every `examples/` program, discovered from
its directory, is compiled under `--json` in both number modes, and any
`"severity":"performance"` object fails the run, naming its
`file:line:col` and `NL9xxx` code. The compiler's own source is not at zero
yet, so `self/compile.ts` is held to `tests/perf-baseline.json` instead: a
count per file and per code, read from the `--json` of the compile the
self-hosting section already makes. More warnings fails and prints the
ones of the file and code that grew; fewer fails until the baseline is
lowered, so the cap only moves down.

The sixteen warnings `std/json` and `std/testing` carried, and the five in
`examples/argv.ts` and `examples/arrays.ts`, are proven away rather than
silenced: guards the bounds proof reads, a string skip written as a flag
in the scanning loop instead of a cursor assigned a callee's answer, a loop
bounded by both lengths it indexes, and an element read into a local
before a call can drop what the loop condition proved. Every answer the
two modules give is unchanged, both still compile under
`--number-mode f64`, and `tests/link/std_json` now pins the nested-string
skip with committed cases.

`tests/nish-cmp.js` now accepts a declared difference's words from the
release section `scripts/changelog-gen.mjs` would render for the commits
since the last release, as well as from `CHANGELOG.md`, so a pull request
names its output change through its own subject instead of a hand-written
`[Unreleased]` line the next release would duplicate. It runs the
generator's own command line without `--write`, fetches the history and
tags a shallow checkout lacks, and fails loudly when the range still
cannot be read.
metrics: std/ and examples/ 21 -> 0 performance warnings; self/compile.ts baseline 89 after #157 (NL9007 69, NL9010 11, NL9009 4, NL9002 3, NL9003 2)
